thesis: Controlled worlds diagnose whether limits arise from information, representation or discovery.
role: Design discrete laboratories with unfavorable controls.

ideas.statement: Counter, stack and changing-regime worlds separate useful supplied structure from autonomous discovery and test unseen lengths and compositions.
Failures must distinguish missing information, failed learning and a representation whose system costs exceed comparators.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: Random-history controls and arbitrary symbol renaming expose invented structure or convenient conventions.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: Cases and criteria must be fixed before evaluation, including unfavorable families; longer sequences with one modulus do not establish general modular arithmetic.

audit.notes: Complete batch read; headings and navigation excluded from idea ranking.
